A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the positive emotions that are associated with fitness-enhancing functions of exploration, play, and affiliation facilitate persuasion, whereas the positive emotions associated with fitness-enhanced functions of awe and nurturance reduce persuasion.

the positive emotions that have a more direct connection to survival (awe and nurturant) tend to reduce persuasion, while positive emotions that are less directly connected to survival (amusement, anticipation, love) tend to facilitate persuasion.

positive emotions can be divided into two groups: those that are more likely to be experienced during social interactions (e.g., attachment love, nurturant love, and awe), and those that are more associated with non-social interactions (e.g. anticipatory enthusiasm, and amusement).

the influence of positive emotions on persuasion processing is emotion specific and can be explained by the different fitness-enhancing functions of different positive emotions.
